instrument_name: Decree on measures to implement the Law on Product and Goods Quality, including goods labels
status: in force (replaced Decree 43/2017 and Decree 111/2021 on goods labels)
relevance_to_alt_protein: High: sets the name, ingredient-quantity and GM wording rules for every packaged protein food
key_provisions: Carries the Decree 43/2017 rules (phrase search): labels truthful and reflecting the true nature of goods; the name must not mislead about nature, use or composition; an ingredient named in the product name must be quantified; GM ingredients marked biến đổi gen beside the ingredient name with its content. Chapter III section 3 covers digital product passports and electronic labels; Art 49(1) sets tolerances for declared nutrients (not read)
notes: Read only to Art 32; the label chapter (IV), Art 49 and the Art 98 transition did not render. Carry-over rests on a customs letter (LBL-08) and exact-phrase index matches (LBL-09). No rule reserves meat or milk words.

instrument_name: Circular on nutrition labelling of foods
relevance_to_alt_protein: Medium: protein content must be printed on every non-exempt pre-packaged food
key_provisions: Pre-packaged foods declare energy, protein, carbohydrate, fat and sodium per 100 g, per 100 ml, per serving or per pack (mandatory since 1 January 2026 under Circular 29/2023, carried over); % of the 50 g protein reference value optional; stock labelled before 1 January 2026 may be sold to expiry; no claim conditions; exempts single-ingredient foods and foods made by small food businesses
notes: Most wet-market chay made by small businesses is exempt (our reading), so lab tests are still needed for those products.

instrument_name: National standard: guidelines for use of nutrition and health claims
relevance_to_alt_protein: High: sets the protein claim conditions a chay or plant product can use
key_provisions: Protein source claim at 10% of the reference value per 100 g (solids), 5% per 100 kcal or 10% per serving; high (cao) claim at twice source; with the 50 g reference value: 5 g and 10 g per 100 g, or 2.5 g and 5 g per 100 kcal (our calculation); comparative claims need a 25% difference; claims require a nutrition panel; health claims need acceptance by the national authority
notes: No per 100 ml protein condition seen in the extracts. A content claim triggers no registration or advertising approval (Decree 15/2018; Decree 342/2025).

instrument_name: National standard: guidelines on nutrition labelling (reference values)
relevance_to_alt_protein: Low to Medium: sets the 50 g protein reference value used for claims

instrument_name: National standard: foods and food ingredients suitable for vegetarians or vegans
relevance_to_alt_protein: Medium: the only national definition of vegetarian and vegan claims
key_provisions: Vegetarian allows egg, milk (lacto types), honey and bee products; vegan excludes every animal-derived input, including additives, flavourings, enzymes, carriers and processing aids; GMP against unintended presence; claim terms such as sản phẩm thuần chay stand beside the trade name
notes: Silent on alliums, Buddhist practice, GMOs, precision fermentation and animal cells, so its chay is broader than Buddhist chay. Two reads differ on whether sản phẩm chay is among the listed terms.

instrument_name: National standards for processed and canned meat
relevance_to_alt_protein: Medium: decide whether a meat product with a plant or fungal extender keeps its name
key_provisions: TCVN 7049 (heat treated) and 7050 (not heat treated) set no minimum meat or protein content and do not mention plant protein; TCVN 7048 (canned meat) lets the maker self-declare the meat share
notes: With no minimum, a 20 to 30% extender keeps the meat name; the named meat must still be quantified under the goods-label rule.

instrument_name: National technical regulation on liquid milk products

notes: No clause reserves sữa for dairy; TCVN 11216:2015 also has no Codex-style restriction on dairy terms (FTR-07).

instrument_name: Joint circular on labelling of pre-packaged genetically modified food
issuer: MARD (now MAE) and Ministry of Science and Technology
relevance_to_alt_protein: High for precision fermentation: sets when a GM label is required
key_provisions: Art 1(1): applies when at least one GM ingredient is more than 5% of total ingredients; Art 1(2): does not apply to GM food in which neither the modified gene nor its product can be detected, to fresh or unpackaged GM food, or in emergencies; Art 4: biến đổi gen beside the ingredient name
notes: Low-dose uses such as lactoferrin at about 0.08% of a formula (LBL-25) are below the trigger. Open: whether a recombinant protein identical to the native protein is a detectable product of the modified gene.

instrument_name: Decree on micronutrient fortification of foods
status: in force (a 2025 amendment draft concerned iodised salt in fish sauce; no amending decree found)
relevance_to_alt_protein: Low to Medium: no protein food is a mandatory vehicle; relevant to a zinc-fortified plant dish for schools
key_provisions: Art 5: iodine, iron, zinc and vitamin A are the mandatory fortificants; Art 6: salt for eating and processing must be iodised; wheat flour used in food processing must carry iron and zinc; soy, palm, rapeseed and peanut oil must carry vitamin A, except oil for industrial processing
notes: Version 0.4 (W8-L4). Tofu, textured soy and soy milk get nothing by rule. A fortified food self-declares under Decree 15/2018 unless it is a special-diet food or for children up to 36 months, which must register.
